text: Build the fluid volume in metres: cylinder + four tangential duct boxes, minus nothing (outlet is just a disk patch on the top).
The geometry cell errored on `is_valid` (a property, not a method), so it never entered the script. Re-emitting it whole, corrected.
The union is right; now the top disk must be imprinted with the 40 mm outlet circle so both share tessellation nodes. Using OCC's `BRepFeat_SplitShape` so the split edge is in the BRep.

Split is exact (outlet 1.257e-3 m² = π·0.02²). Now tessellate the whole solid once with BRepMesh so all faces share edge nodes, and classify every face into a patch by construction data (duct axes), not by bounding box.
All 28 faces classified, none left over. Now write one ASCII STL per patch into `constant/triSurface`, and measure the patch areas against the request.
Weld all patch triangles together and count free edges — this is the closure the check will measure.
Chord error at 0.4 mm is coarse for a 60 mm wall; re-tessellate at 0.1 mm deviation and re-export, reusing the same classifier.
Enough shaping — mesh it. cfMesh `cartesianMesh` takes the multi-solid STL directly and names patches from the solids. Coarse first: 8 mm cells.
`checkMesh` passes at 8 mm, but inlets get only 7 faces each. Refine: 5 mm global, 2.5 mm on the duct/inlet patches so each 20×30 port has ~8×12 faces.
Mesh OK. Now verify the numbers the request named *from the mesh itself*: inlet area, inlet centroid height, and the angle of each inlet face normal off the local tangent.
The angle must be measured against the tangent at the *port on the wall*, not at the inlet's own azimuth. Recomputing with the duct axis from mesh inlet centroid to its wall point.
Inlet area and centroid height carry a ~2 % staircase bias. One refinement pass on the duct patches to tighten the ports.
Ports are within 0.5 % now. A look at the mesh: surface patches plus a clip through the port plane.

Geometry and mesh both check out. Final cell: drop the combined multi-solid STL (it was only cfMesh's input and would duplicate every patch surface in the triSurface directory), leaving exactly one STL per patch.
